questions.q: The formula =A1/B1 shows #DIV/0!. The most likely reason is:
questions.solution: #DIV/0! means the divisor (B1) is zero or blank. Text in A1 would raise #VALUE!; a narrow column shows #####; a misspelt function shows #NAME?.
questions.shortcut: Divide error -> look at the cell below the slash.

questions.q: A page break is inserted in MS Word using:
questions.solution: Ctrl+Enter forces the following text to start on a new page. Ctrl+P prints, Ctrl+B bolds, Alt+Enter has no page-break role in Word.
questions.shortcut: 'Break the page' = press Enter with Ctrl's help: Ctrl+Enter.

questions.q: Which OS service decides which waiting program gets the CPU next?
questions.solution: Process management (scheduling) shares CPU time among ready processes. Memory management allocates RAM, file management handles storage, device management drives peripherals.
questions.shortcut: Verb match: 'gets the CPU' -> process scheduling; 'gets RAM' -> memory management.

questions.q: The Run dialog box, used to launch programs such as 'cmd' or 'calc' by name, opens with:
questions.solution: Win+R opens Run. Win+X opens the Quick Link (power user) menu. Ctrl+R reloads a browser page and does Fill Right in Excel.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The new taxation policy will have a far-reaching ___ on small traders.
questions.solution: After the article *a* the blank must be a noun, and the meaning is 'result': **effect**. *Affect* is the verb; *affection* is fondness; *effectiveness* needs no 'a far-reaching' frame and changes the meaning.

questions.q:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them contains an error. Select the part that contains the error.

The interviewer asked / my friend that why / he had left / his previous job.
questions.solution: After *asked*, the reported clause drops **that** when the question word *why* introduces it: 'asked my friend why he had left'. *That* and *why* cannot introduce the same clause. (The backshift to *had left* in part 3 is correct.)
questions.shortcut: In indirect questions, the wh-word alone introduces the clause — 'asked that why' doubles the introducer.

questions.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number (5).
questions.solution: The city pays residents to *take care of* the trees outside their homes: **look after**. *Look into* means investigate; *look down upon* means despise; *look up to* means admire. Only *look after* names an action whose absence would leave streets un-green and whose payment makes civic sense.
questions.shortcut: Substitute 'tend' — the option surviving the substitution wins.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

To beat about the bush
options: to search carefully in a forest
to avoid coming to the point
questions.solution: Hunters beat *around* bushes to flush game without striking it — skirting the centre. Hence **avoiding the main topic**.
questions.shortcut: Picture: striking the edges, never the centre → dodging the point.

questions.q: In the IPL 2026 final, Royal Challengers Bengaluru defeated —
questions.solution: RCB chased down Gujarat Titans to win by 5 wickets at the Narendra Modi Stadium, Ahmedabad. Punjab Kings were RCB's final opponents in 2025 — the classic wrong option.
questions.shortcut: 2025 final: RCB beat PBKS; 2026 final: RCB beat GT.

questions.q: The motto '**Satyameva Jayate**' on India's national emblem is taken from the —
questions.solution: The words come from the **Mundaka Upanishad** ('Truth alone triumphs'). The emblem itself is adapted from Ashoka's Lion Capital at Sarnath.

questions.q: Two resistors of 6 Ω and 3 Ω are connected in parallel. What is their equivalent resistance?
questions.solution: For two resistors in parallel, R = R₁R₂/(R₁ + R₂) = (6 × 3)/(6 + 3) = 18/9 = **2 Ω**.
questions.shortcut: Parallel result is always smaller than the smallest resistor (3 Ω) — only 2 Ω or 0.5 Ω qualify; product/sum gives 2.

questions.q: The smallest bone in the human body is:
questions.solution: The **stapes** (stirrup) in the **middle ear** is the smallest bone. The femur (thigh bone) is the longest. Malleus and incus are the other two ear ossicles, both larger than the stapes.

questions.q: The population of a village increased by 20% in the first year, by 25% in the second year and by 10% in the third year. If the present population is 66,000, what was it 3 years ago?
The area of a regular hexagon of perimeter 36 cm is:
questions.solution:
Side $=\frac{36}{6}=6$ cm.

Area $=\frac{3\sqrt3}{2}\times6^2=54\sqrt3$ sq cm.
questions.shortcut: Six equilateral triangles: $6\times\frac{\sqrt3}{4}\times36=54\sqrt3$. Trap: $36\sqrt3$ is the equilateral area with side 6... ×6 rule forgotten halfway.

questions.q: The readership of a magazine fell from 4.8 lakh to 4.2 lakh. The percentage decrease is:
How many numbers between 1 and 500 are divisible by 7?
questions.solution: Multiples of 7 below 500: $\lfloor 499/7 \rfloor = 71$ (the largest is $7 \times 71 = 497$).

questions.q: Arrange as in a dictionary: **Angel, Angle, Anger, Amble, Amber.** Which word comes **fourth**?
questions.solution: AM group first (Amber, Amble; B < L), then the ANG group at the 4th letter: Angel (E) and Anger (E) precede Angle (L). Angel vs Anger splits at the 5th: L < R. Order: Amber, Amble, Angel, Anger, Angle → fourth = **Anger**.
questions.shortcut: First-letter split (AM/AN), then compare at the first difference only.

questions.q:
**Statement:** In a class of 50 students, 30 passed in Mathematics and 35 passed in Science. Every student passed in at least one of the two subjects.

**Conclusions:**
I. 15 students passed in both subjects.
II. 20 students passed only in Science.

Which of the conclusions follow(s) from the statement?
questions.solution: Both = 30 + 35 − 50 = 15, so I **follows**. Only Science = 35 − 15 = 20, so II **follows**. Answer: **Both**.
questions.shortcut: n(A∩B) = n(A) + n(B) − total when nobody fails both.

questions.solution: The correct figure sits in the **lower-left part** of the given figure, with every line matching in direction and length. The other three options are the same shape shown as its mirror (left-right flip), a water image (top-bottom flip) and a copy turned through 90 degrees — none of them can be traced in the figure without turning it, and rotation is not allowed.
questions.shortcut: Fix the most distinctive stroke (a lone diagonal or an odd-length line), locate it in the main figure, then check the rest.

questions.q:
**Statements:** All squares are rectangles. No rectangle is a circle.

**Conclusions:** I. No square is a circle. II. Some circles are not squares.
questions.solution: Squares live inside rectangles, and rectangles never meet circles → no square meets a circle: I follows. Circles are non-empty and entirely outside rectangles, hence entirely outside squares → at least one circle is not a square: II follows too. **Both.**
questions.shortcut: A full exile (No) plus non-emptiness gives you a free 'Some … not' conclusion.
